A_FEASIBILITY_FACT_THE_RULING_EXPOSES_CO.why_this_is_here: the ruled N is now 6. Conjunct (a) of the FROZEN decision rule is a UTC-DAY-CLUSTER test, and a clustered sign permutation over G days has a FLOOR -- a most-extreme attainable p of 1/2^G one-sided, 2/2^G two-sided. Holm requires the smallest p <= alpha/m. So for some (G, m, sidedness) cells the primary CANNOT CLEAR NO MATTER WHAT THE DATA SAYS.
A_FEASIBILITY_FACT_THE_RULING_EXPOSES_CO.independently_sourced: the same fact is recorded, in DA's own words and not mine, inside data/pm_5min/derived/da_dayverdict_20260907.json -> race_withdrawal.race_reading: 'At G=5 with the recorded multiplicity 2 the best achievable adjusted p is 0.0625 > 0.05: the ceiling of a clustered permutation test is its floor, 1/2^G.'
A_FEASIBILITY_FACT_THE_RULING_EXPOSES_CO.positive_control: my formula reproduces DA's independently recorded 0.0625 at G=5, m=2, one-sided; a variant ignoring m does not (checked, both directions)
WHAT_IT_SAYS_AT_THE_RULED_G_EQUALS_6: the ruled N=6 clears the arithmetic in EXACTLY ONE CELL: ONE-SIDED and family <= 3.
family 2 is ALREADY WITHDRAWN by amendment 1 (v2, 3fc91e7); my artifact-based LOWER BOUND is 10. At m=10 the adjusted floor is 0.15625 and G=6 CANNOT CLEAR -- it would need G >= 8.
TWO-SIDED, the freeze's own stated posture, does not clear at G=6 for ANY family >= 2: floor 0.0625 > 0.05, needing G >= 7.

THE_SIDEDNESS_QUESTION_I_AM_RAISING_NOT_.the_conflict: the frozen null construction states p is TWO-SIDED, and gives the reason: 'the direction was chosen AFTER the point estimates were seen'. That rationale applies to conjunct (a)'s day-cluster sign test just as it applies to the matched control. DA's cited arithmetic, by contrast, uses the ONE-SIDED floor.
THE_SIDEDNESS_QUESTION_I_AM_RAISING_NOT_.why_it_matters: it is the difference between a primary that can clear and one that cannot: one-sided m<=3 clears at G=6; two-sided does not clear at G=6 for any m>=2.
THE_SIDEDNESS_QUESTION_I_AM_RAISING_NOT_.who_decides: NOT ME. This is the coordinator's to rule with the user, and it must be ruled BEFORE the first day is read, not after -- choosing sidedness once the sign is visible is rule 11.
THE_SIDEDNESS_QUESTION_I_AM_RAISING_NOT_.my_reading_stated_as_a_reading: the freeze's own rationale for two-sidedness is not specific to the control, so I read conjunct (a) as two-sided; under that reading G=6 cannot clear and the ruled population would need a seventh day at family 2, or a ninth at family 10.

A_FEASIBILITY_FACT_THE_RULING_EXPOSES_CO.what_this_does_NOT_do: it does not touch a parameter, and it does not reopen the ruling. N=6 is the population. This records that at N=6 the DECISION RULE may be arithmetically incapable of returning a pass, so that a later reader does not read an INCONCLUSIVE as evidence against the arms when it was foreordained by the floor.
A_FEASIBILITY_FACT_THE_RULING_EXPOSES_CO.the_other_conjunct_is_unaffected: conjunct (b), the generation/side/hour-matched control, pools 500 DRAWS and has floor 1/501 = 0.001996. No feasibility problem there. The floor binds conjunct (a) only.
